# One replay import observer candidate

This is static preparation for root review. The observer has not run. It changes no product or acceptance source and does not replace the failed 39-encounter run. Root must release the sole runtime slot before execution and owns preview startup, process supervision, cleanup, retention and any later decision.

The observer starts the existing production app, opens its Session tools and imports the original `charge-stop-interrupted-replay.json` once through the normal file input and Import replay button. It preserves the original artwork readiness predicate, 20 ms polling and 60,000 ms timeout. It supplies no Play, End, seek or combat input. The application's normal import callback internally verifies the replay before creating its initial tick-zero scene; this unavoidable import behavior is part of the observation. No separate simulation or replay audit runs.

Before opening the browser, the candidate reads the original seal, freeze, first complete dist/public receipt, runtime identity and replay. Their hashes and full pins are fixed in its source. It compares all source/public/proof fingerprints and complete path sets with the original receipt, compares all 398 dist files and their path set, and compares the selected Node, Playwright entry/package and Chromium executable bytes. It executes no checker, builder, fixture producer or game module. The 591-file source footprint and original 398-file dist receipt remain the reference; docs pin `37bf0e794e7f62cf33347d2e92c739d593bf1cc4` is separate from runtime pin `f18a50d904c57ae1652f157b946ebd39d8d8923c`.

The browser retains all `/assets/` requests, response statuses, failures, sizes and SHA-256 values, including PNG and atlas JSON. It also records document/script/stylesheet responses, console warnings/errors and page errors. Each successful response records whether its origin and bytes match an original dist fingerprint. Before any replay input, the observer waits for admitted response tasks and requires the production HTML's declared and all observed executable responses to match the frozen dist. This authenticates the product being driven. Artwork HTTP or decode failures remain diagnostic observations.

Each runtime manifest response is saved byte for byte in the new output. Failed or unavailable response-body reads remain explicit capture errors; each body read has a 15-second bound. At the final capture boundary, the observer unregisters the body-task response handler, records the seal time and drains every admitted task while the browser remains alive. Later responses are recorded separately with status and an explicit `bodyCaptured:false` limit. The receipt is serialized only after the admitted tasks settle and the owned browser closes.

Snapshots record the four readiness terms independently, tick, mode, pause, camera, artwork counts, session notices and complete observed game state. A snapshot follows replay-mode admission and another records the first failure or ready outcome. One screenshot records the final diagnostic view. The private texture/frame maps and internal completeness subconditions are not exposed by the existing app diagnostics; this candidate does not inject hooks or edit the app to read them. Network/console evidence can distinguish some loading and decoding failures, but a clean single import does not explain a failure after many earlier game replacements.

The receipt reports `readinessPassed`, `replayImportAttempts`, `replayModeObserved` and zero playback/seek inputs. The counter records an attempted native import; mode and tick establish whether the replay was admitted. Its `admissions` array remains empty. A passed observation establishes the result of this one import on the authenticated artifact; it does not complete a combat group, stage 07, stage 08 or any feature. A failed observation preserves the first failure without retry or fallback.

The candidate uses only the owned loopback preview at port 5397. It does not start, stop or change a server. Root must confirm the preview serves the unchanged owned dist, supervise the script with the same original stdout/stderr/exit/process receipts, retain the exact reviewed candidate bytes, and drain its owned browser/preview processes afterward. Root's protected PID 1063, port 4173 and 397-file dist must stay unchanged. The active faction run at port 5298 also remains protected until its slot is released.

After review and serial release, the concrete invocation is:

```bash
GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/Cellar/node@24/24.21.0/bin/node /tmp/ovf-f18-replay-observer-v2-tzwrd686/observe-one-replay-import.mjs http://127.0.0.1:5397/ /tmp/ovf-f18-one-replay-observation-NEW
```

Root must choose a fresh external output directory. No runtime is authorized by the presence of this command.
